title: Protocol to detect RNAs from tissue sections in mice using Y-branched probe in situ hybridization
protocol: Sacrifice the animal by cervical dislocation.
Dissect and embed the tissue in O.C.T..
Float a PCR tube rack on the surface of liquid nitrogen.
Place the O.C.T. embedded tissue block on the tube rack.
Wait until O.C.T. solidifies.
Drop the O.C.T. block into liquid nitrogen until there are no more bubbles.
Store the block at −80°C until use.
Section the tissue at 10 μm using a cryostat at −25°C.
Dry slides at 100°C for 2 min.
Add water into the humidifying chamber.
Place the slides into the humid chamber.
Fix slides in 4% PFA for 1 h at room temperature (18°C–25°C).
Wash slides 3× with PBS, 5 min each.
Wash slides with freshly prepared 1-methylimidazole buffer for 5 min.
Fix slides in EDC fixative for 1 h.
Wash slides with PBS for 5 min.
Optional: Permeabilize slides in 100% methanol at room temperature (18°C–25°C) for 1 h.
Remove PBS.
Air dry the slides.
Draw a well around the tissue with ImmEdge hydrophobic barrier PAP pen.
Digest the tissue with 10 μg/mL proteinase K in IDTE buffer for 10 min at 40°C.
Wash slides with PBS for 5 min.
Wash slides with hybridization solution for 5 min.
Prepare probe mixture (4 pmol per probe) by adding 2 μL of each of the odd and even probes (2 μM stock solution) into 1 mL hybridization buffer.
Hybridize sections with probe mixture at 40°C overnight (12–18 h).
Remove probe mixture by flicking the slide to shake off the droplet.
Wash slides in probe wash buffer four times for 30 minutes each at 40°C.
Wash slides in 5× SSCT three times for 5 minutes each at room temperature (18°C–25°C).
Wash slides in hybridization buffer for 5 minutes at room temperature (18°C–25°C).
Mix 5 μL preamplifier (20 ng/μL) with 500 μL probe hybridization buffer to achieve a final concentration of 0.2 ng/μL.
Incubate sections with the preamplifier for 5 hours at 40°C.
Wash slides in probe wash buffer for 30 minutes at 40°C.
Equilibrate sections in amplification buffer for 5 minutes at room temperature (18°C–25°C).
Anneal 2 μL of each HCR hairpin (3 μM) separately in a thermocycler starting at 95°C for 90 seconds, decreasing the temperature by 2°C per minute until reaching 25°C.
Mix both annealed hairpins into 100 μL amplification buffer to achieve a 1:50 dilution.
Incubate sections in hairpin solutions overnight (12–18 h), in the dark, at room temperature (18°C–25°C).
Wash slides in 5× SSCT for 5 min, 3 times.
Mount the coverslip with ProLong gold antifade mounting media.
View the signals under an epifluorescence microscope with a low magnification lens (any 10× or 20× lens) and locate the cells of interest to image.

Image the slides with a confocal microscope using a high magnification lens (Plan-Apochromat 40×/1.4 Oil DIC M27 or Plan-Apochromat 63×/1.4 Oil DIC M27 for Zeiss microscopes, and HC PL APO 100×/1,40 OIL STED WHITE for Leica microscopes).
Empirically determine the laser power to avoid photobleaching.
Take Z-stack images that cover the entire cell of interest.
Use a Z step distance that is half of the z resolution.
Save both individual z images and the maximal intensity projection image.
When multiple areas need to be imaged, use a tile scan to generate a larger image.
Acquire images using a Leica SP8 confocal microscope or a Zeiss 780 confocal microscope when super resolution imaging is not required.
Use super resolution imaging if the density of puncta within cells is too high for regular confocal microscopy.
Zoom into individual punctum and count the number of pixels contained by the punctum to facilitate quantification.
Avoid using resolutions below 5 pixels/μm as it becomes difficult to distinguish individual puncta.
Ensure that the intensities of the brightest and weakest puncta are within the detection range of the sensor.
Adjust system gain, background threshold, and laser power to set a dynamic range with few overexposed or underexposed pixels.
Export images as tiff files for analysis.
